subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should the stale memory-index fix make periodic memory sync default-on for unconfigured users, or should OpenClaw keep `intervalMinutes: 0` and solve watcher silence with a narrower health/restart or opt-in fallback path?
rationale: The source bug is real enough to keep open, but changing the default sync behavior can add background rescans and provider work for existing users, so automation should not choose that product tradeoff alone.

options.title: Repair and accept default-on fallback
options.body: Merge the candidate approach after fixing the known dirty-scoping conflict and explicitly accepting the 30-minute default as the upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep periodic sync opt-in
options.body: Leave `intervalMinutes` disabled by default and document or doctor-suggest the interval workaround while fixing watcher liveness separately.

options.title: Replace with watcher health recovery
options.body: Close or supersede the current PR with a design that logs, restarts, or verifies watcher liveness without changing the default periodic-sync contract.

recommendation.title: Repair and accept default-on fallback
recommendation.body: Merge the candidate approach after fixing the known dirty-scoping conflict and explicitly accepting the 30-minute default as the upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The memory plugin/config refactor history makes steipete the best available owner for the product boundary and upgrade-default decision.
